review_policy: reviewed means every capture cited for the operation replays against the node with no difference and at least one is cited, for the cases those captures cover; it never means exhaustive equivalence. known_gap names a difference a replay observes, and the capture's replay lists it exactly. not_reviewed means the cited captures, if any, don't settle the operation, even if the node routes it.

deliberate_gaps.timestamped-signatures-only: Every signed operation: upstream also accepts a request whose auth chain signs only its method and its path below /v1 (lowercased), whatever x-identity-timestamp or x-identity-metadata header the request carries or omits, valid until the delegated key expires. The node accepts only the timestamped payload over its own method and path, at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses such a request with upstream's 401 {ok:false, data:{message}, error:'Unauthenticated'}.
deliberate_gaps.signature-window: Every signed operation: upstream accepts a timestamp up to 30 minutes old or ahead; the node accepts at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses the rest with the same 401.
deliberate_gaps.unauthenticated-message: Every signed operation: when a signature does not verify, upstream's data.message is its verifier's own text, which includes the payload it expected and its local clock; the node's is a fixed text naming the failed check (Invalid auth chain, Invalid timestamp, Expired signature, Invalid signature). The status, error and envelope are upstream's, and no client reads data.message.
deliberate_gaps.chain-copy-lag: Every operation that reads a collection's published or approved state: upstream asks the Polygon collections subgraph on each request; the node reads its copy of that subgraph, which the shop's collections mirror refreshes every three times MARKETPLACE_MIRROR_INTERVAL_SECS (15 minutes at the default 300). A collection deployed outside the node's own publication flow reads as unpublished, and an approval or a role change as not yet made, until the next pass, so a client that polls after a deployment (the old builder web retries its publish every 5 seconds) waits up to that bound plus the subgraph's lag. When the copy has no complete pass the node answers 503, and when its last pass, or the row or absence a decision reads, is more than 30 minutes old it answers 503 to every request that grants access or writes.
deliberate_gaps.owner-is-the-chain-creator: Every operation that decides by a standard collection's owner: once the node's copy of the Polygon collections subgraph holds the collection, its owner is the chain creator for every check; before, the stored eth_address. Upstream compares the stored eth_address in some checks and the chain creator in others until an owner sync rewrites the row, so between a creator transfer and that sync a client of upstream sees the previous creator keep, and the new creator lack, part of the owner's access; the node gives all of it to the chain creator at once.
deliberate_gaps.managers-from-chain-only: Every operation that admits an on-chain manager: the node reads managers only from its copy of the Polygon collections subgraph, so only a collection on chain has managers. Upstream also admits the managers a PUT /v1/collections/:id body stored for a collection that is not on chain.
deliberate_gaps.access-checks-never-write: DELETE /v1/items/:id and POST /v1/items/:id/files: the node's access check changes no row. Upstream's can set a collection's stored eth_address, and its items', to the chain creator when they differ, so a later read of those rows names the creator.
deliberate_gaps.access-before-kind-conflict: PUT /v1/collections/:id on an existing collection: the node answers 401 Unauthorized to upsert collection before it compares the body's URN with the stored collection, so only a signer who may save the collection gets the 409s for converting it or changing its third party. Upstream answers those 409s first.
deliberate_gaps.committee-cache: GET /v1/committee: the node answers from the same read of the Polygon collections subgraph its committee decisions use, kept one hour, so a member added or removed shows up to an hour later. Upstream reads the subgraph on every GET /v1/committee and keeps its own read an hour for decisions.
deliberate_gaps.committee-unavailable: Every operation a committee member may perform: when the Polygon collections subgraph can't answer, the node answers 503 to GET /v1/committee and to every decision only the committee could grant, and asks again after 30 seconds. Once its read is more than an hour old and a refresh has failed, a committee member reads published content as any signer does until a read succeeds. Upstream answers GET /v1/committee with an empty list and treats nobody as a member.
